scoring_justification: T1: recompute SFE (q=1) and unstable SFE (max relaxed) from gsf_energy.csv; structural audit interlayer spacing trends; reference-match summary values against paper gold with tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Hidden gold for SFE, unstable SFE, c/a, and interlayer trend specifications.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table I, Fig.2, and inline text. Pd relaxed SFE=225, unstable SFE=383 mJ/m²; Pt relaxed SFE=339, unstable SFE=432 mJ/m²; c/a values 1.632 (Pd) and 1.620 (Pt); interlayer trends: Pd first contracts, third expands, second expands then contracts; Pt first+second contract, third expands.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from paper; tolerances set to ~50-60 mJ/m² for energies (typical expected spread for tight-binding implementation) and 0.02 for c/a.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are taken verbatim from the paper's reported results and physical constants; they are not invented.

outputs.description: Generalized stacking fault energy curve (relaxed and unrelaxed) as a function of stacking fault variable q. The checker will recompute SFE (energy at q=1) and unstable SFE (maximum relaxed energy) from this file and compare to hidden paper-reported values within tolerances.
Interlayer spacing changes vs q for the first, second, and third layers. The checker will audit qualitative trends (e.g., expansion/contraction patterns).
Summary of SFE, unstable SFE, and c/a ratio at the stacking fault. Checker compares these values to hidden paper-reported references within tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The tight-binding solver must be implemented or adapted from an open-source code (e.g., pyscf, sisl, or a custom NRL-TB implementation). The original Mehl TB code is proprietary; the agent is expected to use an equivalent open-source engine. All results are computed from scratch; no pre-made intermediate files are provided.

steps.description: Recompute relaxed SFE (q=1) and unstable SFE (max relaxed) for Pd and Pt from gsf_energy.csv; compare to paper gold with absolute tolerances.
Structural audit: verify qualitative interlayer spacing trends for Pd (first contracts, third expands, second expands then contracts) and Pt (first+second contract, third expands).
Reference match: compare reported SFE, unstable SFE, and c/a for each metal to paper gold with tolerances.
